title: Minimal Polynomial Reduction Theorem
content:
The core theorem: evaluating any polynomial f at matrix M equals evaluating the remainder of f modulo the minimal polynomial. This is analogous to modular arithmetic: just as a mod n captures all information about a in Z/nZ, the remainder f mod minpoly captures all information about aeval M f.

The proof uses the division algorithm: f = q * minpoly + r, then aeval M f = aeval M q * aeval M minpoly + aeval M r = 0 + aeval M r.

title: Degree Bound: Tighter than Charpoly
content: The reduced polynomial has degree < deg(minpoly) <= deg(charpoly) = n. For derogatory matrices, deg(minpoly) < n, giving a strictly tighter bound. For example, a scalar matrix cI has minpoly = X - c (degree 1), while charpoly = (X - c)^n (degree n).

title: Annihilator Ideal Characterization
content: The key structural result: aeval M f = 0 if and only if minpoly divides f. This means the annihilator of M in K[X] is exactly the principal ideal (minpoly). Since K[X] is a PID, every ideal is principal, and the minimal polynomial is the unique monic generator of the annihilator ideal.

title: Congruence Classes
content: Two polynomials f and g evaluate to the same matrix if and only if minpoly divides (f - g). This defines an equivalence relation: f ~ g mod minpoly. The quotient ring K[X]/(minpoly) is isomorphic to the subalgebra of matrices generated by M, with dimension equal to deg(minpoly).

title: Power Reduction
content: Every matrix power M^k can be expressed as a linear combination of I, M, M^2, ..., M^{d-1} where d = deg(minpoly). This is the key to efficient matrix function computation: instead of computing M^100 directly, reduce X^100 mod minpoly to get a polynomial of degree < d.

title: Charpoly Reduction Refines to Minpoly
content: Any reduction done via the characteristic polynomial can be further refined via the minimal polynomial. Since minpoly | charpoly, the minpoly reduction is at least as tight. This theorem shows the two-step process (reduce mod charpoly, then mod minpoly) gives the same result as directly reducing mod minpoly.

title: Idempotent Matrix Classification
content: If M^2 = M, then M satisfies X^2 - X = X(X-1). Since X(X-1) factors into distinct linear factors over any field, the minimal polynomial of M must be one of: X (if M = 0), X-1 (if M = I), or X(X-1) (otherwise). This trichotomy classifies idempotent matrices by their minimal polynomial.

title: Nilpotency via Minimal Polynomial
content: A matrix is nilpotent if and only if its minimal polynomial is X^d for some d. The nilpotency index (smallest d with M^d = 0) equals the degree of the minimal polynomial. This is more precise than using the characteristic polynomial: charpoly = X^n always has degree n, but minpoly = X^d can have d << n.
